newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia moves towards private school education.
newsitem.headline: Australia moves towards private school education.

text.p: Australia moved more towards private education last year, with enrolments for non-government schools growing faster than for government institutions.
The number of full-time students attending Australia's non-government schools rose 2.2 percent to 921,458 in 1996 from 901,484 the previous year, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said on Tuesday.
This compared with a rise of only 0.6 percent in full-time students attending government schools to 2.22 million in 1996 from 2.21 million the previous year, the bureau said.
The number of government schools fell 0.5 percent to 7,088 since August 1995, while the number of private schools rose 0.6 percent to 2,542.
There were 3.14 million students in Australia's 9,630 primary and secondary schools in August 1996, compared with 3.11 million full-time students attending 9,648 schools operating in 1995.
